The magic of universal translators. Obviously, it cuts through some boring elements that get in the way of a good narrative, but (especially in first contact scenarios) it often feels like a convenient solution. Aliens should be *alien* and not just quirky human-like characters in costumes. One of my favorite treatments of the subject of alien life is a classic story where the characters look directly at it several times and still don't understand what it is. In fact, they continue to learn about it all the way through to the end of the story.

Another aspect that bothers me is the prevalence of various Dominions, Alliances, and Federations. It's hard to avoid clichés all the time, but extraterrestrial politics should have a *little* more variety.

Also, the use of expendable characters with no real narrative function other than to increase the kill count for the hero. And the intimidating soldiers that can never seem to hit anything. That was one of the things that made a recent film so terrific; the soldiers can actually *aim* for once. The trope of defeat in detail is a cliché in just about every corny martial arts movie. Instead of swarming the hero all at once, a dozen antagonists line up and get defeated one by one.

As for things I like... I have to say that few things are more entertaining than humans brawling with aliens using just their bare hands. I feel a bit ridiculous saying that, but I can't help it. Few things define the spirit of humanity quite like an alien taking a hit (or a hit equivalent). A certain blockbuster was a terrible movie, but the scene where the protagonist punches the alien pilot almost made the whole thing worth it. It's a tricky balance narratively, however. An opponent isn't scary if you know you can defeat them without breaking a sweat. And having the ability to inflict that kind of overwhelming violence should lead to some sort of moral dilemma, unless you're trying to portray the human character as a sociopath.

Aliens recoiling in horror at humans getting drunk or engaging in other behaviors is fun too. A certain substance is such a cliché that it has its own wiki entry, but it really is one of the things that sets us apart right here on Earth in real life.

They have a finite amount of time (three hours?) to get a massive number of personnel to battle stations and launched. It'd be kind of like a naval vessel trying to scramble its entire complement of ~100 aircraft while the ship is sinking or something. There'd be a massive traffic jam at whatever internal chokepoints exist. And at some point, the infrastructure damage will start interfering with continuing to launch units (power outage? fire? significant electromagnetic pulse? decompression taking critical machinery offline?). I wouldn't expect the aggressive faction to be very diligent about something like keeping up-to-date contingency plans and procedures for abandoning their base.
